title.narrative: Development of the Northern Chu and Southern Ma Rivers Irrigation System Project

description.narrative: The project is part of a wider government investment to deliver water from the Cua Dat reservoir to the command area. It will finance the construction and upgrading of about 58 km of main canals (the north and south main canals of the Northern Chu and Southern Ma Rivers Irrigation System--NCSMRIS) and lower order canal distribution systems to supply existing pumped irrigation schemes which presently draw water from the Chu and Ma rivers. It will also to develop presently rainfed areas to serve an irrigation service area of about 23,900 hectares. The project will support capacity building of the irrigation management companies and water user associations to improve operation and management (O&M) of the irrigation system, and provide extension services to farmers. The project will benefit about 120,000 farm families. The government has agreed to comply with ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement for the whole investment program to strengthen the application of social and environmental safeguard procedures.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President
Reports and Recommendations of the President
Loan 2828: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 17 Jun 2022

Progress Toward Outcome: All consultants were mobilized and completed their services on 31 December 2018. The irrigation systems are operated and promoted water supply efficiency from 2018. For technical trainings in WUG management and O&M, Agricultural Extension and GIS, the total number of trainees was 3,295 of which 1,499 were women (44%).
Some results are in the Combined Resettlement Plan and Indigenous Peoples Plans | Sep 2015: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents//40239-013-remdp-03.pdf
Some results are in the Environmental and Social Monitoring Reports | Oct 2018: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/40239/40239-013-esmr-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Nov 2013: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents//40239-013-rp-01.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | May 2019: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/40239/40239-013-sddr-en_1.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1:
Continuous reporting on physical progress is being done on Web GIS which was uploaded to the website in the link: adb6.vnims.vn. Monthly reports from PPMU and ICMB3 are monthly uploaded to the website to ADSB6 website (http://adb6.cpo.vn/default.aspx).
GIS was developed for both Phase 1&2. GIS for Phase 3 is under development. CPO, PPMU, and Nam Song Ma IMC plan to integrate GIS in Phase 3 into the current GIS for Phase 1&2. The system is under final test runs and will be fully functional in the last quarter of 2019. ISF is collected from farmers for financing O&M of on-farm canals. Irrigation management companies prepared the annual business plans. O&M cost is subsidized by the irrigation service fees. 18% of the WUG representatives are women.
Output 2:
13,065.1 ha were irrigated by gravity; 4,099.1 ha were irrigated by pump; and 79.8 ha were rainfed. The initial command area estimate of 23,899 ha was reduced to 17,244.5 ha based on information from more detailed surveys that can be covered with gravity rather than pumped irrigation, while Thuong Xuan District is being covered under Phase 1 and most of Thieu Hoa District being covered under Phase 3. Unskilled laborers: 13,281; Local unskilled laborers 12,260 (92%); Women, 5,024 (38%). Interviewed Ngoc Lac Women's Union and WUGs showed that construction work is not suitable for women, so they mainly participated as cooks or assistants.
Output 3:
Consultant extension package covered 5,241 farmers (8.7%) of which 57.1% were women. The Pilot site for Maize (12 ha) was in operation since January 2017.
Output 4:
Irrigation project was completed within budget. At least 30% of central project management unit and provincial project management unit staff are women. Gender-sensitive training was provided to project staff.
